note: FIRST SOCO KEEPER, REGISTERED 2026-09-16 (lane SOCO-40). There is no predecessor — this is the first SOCO solve of any kind, so nothing is superseded and rule 35 [R-PROMOTE] has nothing to prune. DETERMINATION NOT-YET (rubric v3.8, PRICE UNSCORED), and it is the keeper anyway under rule 1 [R-STRUCT]: it is the most structurally faithful SOCO run that exists, and a determination is not a promotion test. THE DEFINING CONSTRAINT: SOCO HAS NO PRICE BENCHMARK AND NEVER WILL. Its footprint publishes no LMP, hub or clearing price, so data/raw/_validation-source/actual_lmp.json carries NO SOCO block and MUST NOT GAIN ONE — a placeholder would break calibration_verdict._price_reference_absent and silently move SOCO onto the ordinary determination path. C3a / C3b / C3c are UNSCORABLE, NOT FAILED. The ceiling is PHYSICALLY-CALIBRATED (PRICE UNSCORED) and SOCO can NEVER read CALIBRATED. Gate G17 stands absolutely: no neighbouring hub, no proxy, no cost-stack price, ever. The model's own load-weighted mean LMP (33.32 / 31.14 / 199.34 $/MWh) is MODEL-ONLY and UNVERIFIED and is never quoted as price skill. THE RECIPE: the CLI's all-defaults ISO-agnostic backcast construction, 28 non-default ScenarioConfig fields, no --set and no --offer-curve-json, on three geographic zones (SOCO_AL / SOCO_GA / SOCO_MS) over measured FERC-714 shares from the FIVE fully-cited respondents, Tier-3 documented non-binding links (24,400 / 4,300 MW, both measured at dual 0.000), served measured EIA-930 interchange, VOLL 61,900. EVERY offer_curve_by_group BAND IS EXACTLY 1.0 on all 13 groups, offer_curve_overrides and offer_curve_deltas are null, and authorized_price_tuning is declared NONE — the rule 1 [R-STRUCT] authorized channel is not merely unused but unreachable here, since with no price benchmark there is no residual to tune against. There is no soco.py offer-curve delta module; SOCO rides the pure ISO-agnostic GENERIC_BASE_OFFER_CURVE, so rule 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE]'s neutral-fallback requirement holds by construction. THE OWNER'S COAL-SPLIT INSTRUCTION IS WHAT THIS KEEPER EXECUTES, verbatim: "Coal should be split into types. Completely eliminate the single coal class." Done zero-LP by scripts/data/derive_coal_supply.py --iso SOCO --census-vintage 2023 2024 2025, which wrote six rows to data/raw/_processed-legacy/coal_supply_SOCO.csv (Barry 3 / Gaston 26 / Bowen 703 bituminous; Miller 6002 / Daniel 6073 / Scherer 6257 prb) — every SOCO coal plant resolves, COAL_BIT 5,150.5 MW and COAL_PRB 6,361.5 MW measured on the fleet, bare COAL 0.0 MW. Machine-verified on all three class_hourly parquets: every year carries COAL_BIT and COAL_PRB and NO bare COAL. It is a RECLASSIFICATION, not a re-dispatch — every non-coal class is byte-identical to the unsplit arm, the two coal classes sum to the unsplit COAL to the GWh (33.142 / 34.676 / 47.662), and the 2023 and 2024 P0 objectives are identical to the cent (3690944814.1196 / 3398767416.6013); only 2025's moves (5682126660.3872 -> 5680277825.0155), in the scarcity hours its hydro hole creates. WHAT IT BOUGHT: C1's failing rows fall from SEVEN to ONE. Every coal row now passes, because the benchmark scores coal on EIA-923 fuel codes and the model was previously offering one blended class against two benchmark rows (the SPP-40 §7.3 defect) — 2024 COAL_BIT now lands at 12.256 TWh against 12.257 actual. THE GATES: C1 FAIL (1 row of 14; C1 all 13/14, free 9/10), C2 PASS, C4 PASS, C6 PASS, C8 PASS; C3a / C3b / C3c SKIPPED-UNSCORABLE; C5a is REPORTED-ONLY (-5.3 / -8.9 / +4.9 %) and contributes no status. grade_summary 4 of 5 scored, 1 fail, 0 ledgered and 0 protective caveats. THE ONE GATING DEFECT, RECORDED AT REGISTRATION AND NOT ABSORBED: 2023 CT_PEAKER +8.221 TWh (share +3.4pp). It is one half of a near-offsetting MERIT-ORDER MISALLOCATION inside the peaking fleet — CT_PEAKER +8.221 / +4.933 / +7.867 TWh against ST_GAS -6.487 / -4.996 / -4.584 in 2023 / 2024 / 2025. The LP sends energy to combustion turbines that the real system sent to gas steam units. This is SOCO's FIRST LEVER and is queued ahead of SOCO-54/55/56/57; it was NOT tuned around, and no band was touched to move it (rule 1). OTHER DEFECTS CARRIED, NOT ABSORBED: (1) the 2025 EIA-923 HYDRO INPUT HOLE, named in PRECOMMIT §4.5 BEFORE the solve — 5 plants / 0.327 TWh resolve against 6.012 TWh measured, where 2023/2024 resolve 42 plants; coal backfills it (2025 coal 47.66 vs 44.08 actual) and the LP posts 8,930 MWh of slack at VOLL in 13 summer afternoon hours, which is what drags the 2025 MODEL-ONLY mean price to 199.34 $/MWh. NO repair was armed: --hydro-backfill-year and --hydro-eia930-monthly were deliberately not passed, because arming a one-year input repair inside the first keeper is a desk-queue lever decision, not this lane's. Routed as SOCO's next data-intake item. (2) D-1 diurnal shape FAILs (non-gating; rule 20's shape leg is unreachable here because C8 forced share is 0.0 %): 2023 COAL_BIT profile_r 0.622 and cv_ratio 0.015, 2024 COAL_BIT cv_ratio 0.410, 2025 CT_PEAKER cv_ratio 0.466. WHAT THE LANE ACTUALLY ESTABLISHED, and it outlives the arm: the CT_PEAKER/ST_GAS misallocation is NOT a cost-side defect at all. WHY IT IS THE KEEPER -- rule 14 [R-ACCURATE] and rule 1 [R-STRUCT], never the residual. eGRID joins heat rate at PLANT grain (PLNT23.PLHTRT), so every generator at a multi-technology plant inherits one generation-weighted blend: Victor J Daniel Jr (6073) priced 1,004.0 MW of coal at 8.399 MMBtu/MWh -- which NO coal boiler can physically attain, its own meter reading 12.895 -- and Barry (3) priced 1,118.5 MW of coal + 1,821.2 MW of gas CC + 160.0 MW of gas steam all at 8.994965. The construction is each prime-mover family's own sum(UNT23.HTIAN)/sum(GEN23.GENNTAN) from the SAME eGRID vintage the plant-grain join reads: a finer read of the identical source on the identical boundary, zero degrees of freedom. It moves 24 generator rows / 6,473.2 MW at FOUR plants (Barry 3, Greene County 10, Jack Watson 2049, Victor J Daniel Jr 6073). THIS LANE REPAIRED THE MECHANISM'S CONSTRUCTION BEFORE ARMING IT, and that is the lane's real product. The derive's central claim -- that the family rate replaces the blend on the identical net-annual boundary -- is an IDENTITY (sum HTIAN / sum GENNTAN == PLHTRT) and is now CHECKED. Over SOCO's nine covered plants it partitions them with three orders of magnitude to spare: FOUR recompose at ratio 1.000 and FIVE at 4.05-8.40. The five are cogeneration paper mills, where eGRID STEAM-CREDITS PLHTIAN and does NOT steam-credit the unit sheet's HTIAN, so a family rate there charges the host's process steam to the electric output (Pensacola Florida Plant recomposes to 22.537 against a published 5.568). The pre-existing out_of_window guard is a per-FAMILY plausibility test and caught ONLY the steam halves; the TURBINE halves landed INSIDE 3,000-30,000 Btu/kWh and WERE BEING APPLIED -- four rows, 160.0 MW, onto CT_CHP and CC_CHP, the latter a scored C1 row. That is rule 14's misalignment exception verbatim, so a per-PLANT boundary_mismatch flag now refuses them and SOCO's artifact goes 12 applied -> 8. The guard is DERIVE-SIDE, never consumer-side: a guard inside _apply_egrid_family_heat_rates is default-on and would have moved CAISO's keeper fleet from this lane (rule 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE]). NO src/market_sim FILE IS TOUCHED. BOUNDARY_IDENTITY_TOL = 0.005 is a rounding allowance incapable of being tuned: over all 26 covered plants in the three ISOs carrying an artifact the passing side sits at 1.0000 and the failing side starts at 2.800, so every value in (0.001, 1.8) gives the identical partition. Declared ex ante and never swept. RULE 19 [R-ONE-MECH], MACHINE-VERIFIED: precedence is structural, not declared. The family rate is applied at FRAME level in _rows_to_generators; measured_ct_heat_rates is applied inside the ROW LOOP gated on group == 'CT_PEAKER'. So measured CAMPD > eGRID family > eGRID plant blend, and CT_PEAKER's cap-weighted heat rate is BYTE-IDENTICAL at 11.2666 on both sides -- Greene County's computed GT family rate (14.105) and Watson's (21.925) are both entirely overwritten. Nothing is priced twice. CC_CHP / CT_CHP / ST_CHP heat rates are byte-identical too, by the boundary guard. THE GATES ARE FLAT, WHICH IS A STRONGER CASE THAN THE OWNER'S STANDARD REQUIRED: C1 all 12/14 and free 8/10 on BOTH sides, the SAME two rows fail (2023 CT_PEAKER, 2023 ST_GAS), C2/C4/C6/C8 PASS on both, 0 ledgered and 0 protective caveats on both, grade_summary identical, and NO row changes status in either direction. Magnitudes: 2023 CT_PEAKER +9.85 -> +10.09 TWh, 2023 ST_GAS -7.34 -> -7.36; C2's ungated 2025 coal row IMPROVES +16.0% -> +12.4%. C5a is REPORTED-ONLY and contributes no status (2024 -9.0% -> -10.0%). THE EFFECT WAS PREDICTED BEFORE THE SOLVE AND CONFIRMED, INCLUDING THE PART THAT IS UNFLATTERING: PRECOMMIT section 2.2 registered that coal would fall, CC_REGULAR would rise, and that CT_PEAKER and ST_GAS would NOT materially improve -- so THIS ARM DOES NOT FIX SOCO'S HEADLINE DEFECT, and the PRECOMMIT said so rather than the FINDING saying it afterwards. Delivered: COAL -0.665 / -1.855 / -1.528 TWh, CC_REGULAR +0.468 / +1.915 / +1.947, CT_PEAKER +0.234 / +0.399 / +0.157 (inside the declared 1.0 TWh falsifier F2). TWO PREDICTIONS WERE IMPRECISE AND ARE RECORDED AS SUCH: the coal fall was OVER-predicted (2-5 TWh registered, 0.7-1.9 delivered), and the flagged 2024 CC_REGULAR break did NOT occur (+5.38 TWh against a +-7.47 band). Why CT barely moves is measured, not asserted: CC_REGULAR sits at >= 99 % of its own annual maximum in only 44 of the 7,305 hours CT_PEAKER runs in 2023 (3 of 6,447 in 2024; 15 of 7,343 in 2025), so CT's over-run is a COMMITMENT defect and no cost change at four other plants can reach it.
